digest.component_or_area: import bulk path optimization (import_ndjson, event_append, staging, author caching)
propositions: The N=3000 import benchmark makes 6,000 subprocess git-config user.name lookups (47.79s) via author() called once per envelope in append_event; caching within an explicit import context reduces this to one lookup while preserving live behavior for independent interactive writes.

The batch_stage_and_commit path calls sweep_stale_staging once per new CREATE ticket (3,000 times) rescanning the same staging root 375,876 times; sweeping exactly once per bounded batch after the first new ticket reduces this to 12 sweeps for the N=3000 case while preserving sweep behavior for direct/existing-ticket-only batches.

A controlled A/B harness preserving 3,000 creates, 3,000 comments, and 24 commits demonstrates 60.827s (78.8%) wall-time elimination by replacing only the git-config lookup and sweep mechanisms, excluding serialization/commit-count alternatives.

Author caching must use a copy-on-write contextvar scoped to import_tickets to prevent cache leakage across calls, threads, tasks, or pytest sessions while allowing nested contexts and preserving fallback-key parity for git-config-less lookups.
The stage_event sweep optimization must preserve crash-resume, rollback, atomic staging/publish, and all platform coverage; existing-ticket-only and empty batches must not gain stale-sweep work.

Integration oracle must record exactly one user.name lookup and 12 stale sweeps (half of 24 commits) as deterministic counts independent of wall-clock thresholds; independent defect mutations must return RED and prove these mechanisms dominate the observed latency.
